title: Shard-aware quasi-contiguous KV packing and spectral rebalancer
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Production workloads show growing intra-GPU fragmentation in our token KV caches when mixing long-lived prefixes (system prompts, embeddings) with high-churn per-request state. This leads to reduced effective capacity, more evictions, and unpredictable latency spikes during background compaction. Goal: introduce a KV allocation strategy and low-cost background rebalancer that reduces fragmentation without regressing tail latency or increasing per-token cost significantly. The approach must integrate with continuous batching (batch-aware placement) and respect dedicated/Dedicated/Private deployment constraints (minimal extra memory passes, no global stop-the-world rewrites).
proposed_solution: 1) Quasi-contiguous packing: allocate hot shards into 'packing lanes' that prefer contiguous slot ranges but allow controlled islanding to avoid expensive moves. Lanes are sized based on observed prefix-length distributions and per-shard hotness. 2) Soft anchors: mark long-lived tokens with soft anchors (lightweight metadata) that bias placement and avoid relocating anchors unless necessary. 3) Spectral rebalancer: a low-priority background process that computes a spectral occupancy heatmap per GPU (time-decayed access frequency) and identifies low-cost local relocations that yield high fragmentation reduction per byte-moved. Rebalancer operates under a strict CPU/GPU budget and uses incremental micro-swaps (swap small token groups between nearby lanes) to keep latency impact minimal. 4) Batch-aware eviction hints: continuous batching runtime emits affinities for tokens in an incoming batch so allocation can co-locate likely-reused items, increasing cache hit-rate for the batch. 5) Safety: all relocations are KV-atomic with a two-phase handoff and write-through guard to S3-backed cold store if movement fails. Implementation will extend the existing KV index (minimal schema change) and add a lightweight per-GPU rebalancer thread with tunables for budget and aggressiveness.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Extra metadata (anchors/lanes) increases index footprint; mitigated by compact encoding and TTL for anchors.
- Rebalancer may consume CPU/GPU cycles; we limit by budget and schedule during low-percentile load windows.
- Micro-swaps reduce fragmentation but may slightly increase short-term eviction churn; acceptance criteria require no tail-latency regressions.
- Complexity: cross-GPU moves are avoided to keep the design local; multi-GPU defrag reserved for a follow-up if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation ratio (wasted slots / total slots) reduced by >= 30% on mixed workloads compared to baseline for 99th-percentile of trials
No regression in 99.9th percentile token-serving latency (> 0.5% allowed variance) under standard load profile
End-to-end per-token cost change within +/-3% for steady workloads
PR with unit+integration tests and canary rollout to limited Dedicated pool
Observability: dashboard panels for lane occupancy, swap counts, anchor churn, and rebalancer CPU usage available in Console
